title: Flatness of a supplied finite depth-two extension over a smooth local base
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian local ring with closed point $a$ and depth at least two [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-pbc-depth]. Let $q:L\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $U\subset L$ be open, contain every point not lying over $a$, and have dense inverse image in the scheme-theoretic closed fibre $L_a$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $p:E\to L$ be a supplied finite morphism, etale upon restriction over $U$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Assume depth $\mathcal O_{E,z}\geq2$ whenever $p(z)\notin U$. Then $p$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Etaleness is not asserted by this statement. The statement asserts no existence of E and no construction of an extension.

proof.text: Smoothness gives local finite type, so L is locally Noetherian over Spec A. Apply the finite target-flat-locus theorem to obtain an open F of points y such that every source stalk over y is flat. For y in U, transport Flat.stalkMap of the etale restriction p restricted to U through morphismRestrictStalkMap. This proves U is contained in F.

In the closed fibre, let B be the inverse image of the complement of F. Continuity makes B closed. The fibre is Jacobson by local finite type over the residue field. If B is nonempty, Mathlib nonempty_inter_closedPoints produces a closed point x in B. Since U is contained in F, its image is outside U. For every z over this image, apply the closed-fibre formal flatness calculation, contradicting membership in B. Thus B is empty.

For any z in E, if q(p(z)) is not the closed point, haway puts p(z) in U and therefore F. Otherwise use fiberHomeo to lift p(z) to the closed fibre. Its nonmembership in F would put this lift in the empty B. Thus every stalk map is flat. Apply Flat.of_stalkMap to conclude global flatness. All statements, universes and hypotheses are unchanged.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0EYB, separating the closed-point formal-completion calculation from the global flat-locus argument; affine flat-locus proof from the upstream Noetherian flat-locus theorem and explicit Jacobson closed-fibre assembly in Lean
